Chapter: 8th Ch13 - Our Home: Earth, a Unique Life Sustaining Planet
True Statement: All life on Earth exists within the very thin outermost layer of the planet, called the crust.
False 1: All life on Earth exists within the mantle, a thick layer beneath the surface.

Chapter: 8th Ch13 - Our Home: Earth, a Unique Life Sustaining Planet
True Statement: Venus is the hottest planet — not because it is the closest to the Sun — but because its thick atmosphere (almost entirely carbon dioxide) traps heat through the greenhouse effect.
False 1: Venus is the hottest planet because it is the closest to the Sun.
False 2: Mercury is the hottest planet because its thick atmosphere traps heat through the greenhouse effect.

Chapter: 8th Ch13 - Our Home: Earth, a Unique Life Sustaining Planet
True Statement: The greenhouse effect plays an important role in maintaining the right temperature on Earth by trapping heat in the atmosphere.
False 1: The ozone layer plays an important role in maintaining the right temperature on Earth by trapping heat in the atmosphere.

Chapter: 8th Ch13 - Our Home: Earth, a Unique Life Sustaining Planet
True Statement: Earth is at the right distance from the Sun where water can exist in liquid form; this range of distances is called the habitable zone or Goldilocks zone.
False 1: Mars is in the habitable zone (Goldilocks zone) where water exists in liquid form.

Chapter: 8th Ch13 - Our Home: Earth, a Unique Life Sustaining Planet
True Statement: If Earth were closer to the Sun, all water would evaporate; if it were farther away, all water would freeze.
False 1: If Earth were closer to the Sun, all water would freeze; if farther away, all water would evaporate.

Chapter: 8th Ch13 - Our Home: Earth, a Unique Life Sustaining Planet
True Statement: The vast amount of water on Earth makes it look blue from space — hence it is called the Blue Planet.
False 1: The vast amount of forest on Earth makes it look blue from space — hence it is called the Blue Planet.

Chapter: 8th Ch13 - Our Home: Earth, a Unique Life Sustaining Planet
True Statement: Water covers about 70 per cent of Earth's surface.
False 1: Water covers about 30 per cent of Earth's surface.

Chapter: 8th Ch13 - Our Home: Earth, a Unique Life Sustaining Planet
True Statement: Earth orbits the Sun in a nearly circular orbit, keeping sunlight and heat nearly steady throughout the year.
False 1: Earth orbits the Sun in a highly elliptical orbit, causing extreme seasonal temperature variations.

Chapter: 8th Ch13 - Our Home: Earth, a Unique Life Sustaining Planet
True Statement: On Mars, the atmosphere is 100 times thinner than on Earth; Mercury has no atmosphere at all.
False 1: On Mars, there is no atmosphere at all; Mercury has an atmosphere 100 times thinner than Earth.

Chapter: 8th Ch13 - Our Home: Earth, a Unique Life Sustaining Planet
True Statement: Some oxygen in the atmosphere gets converted to ozone — a three-atom oxygen molecule — forming the ozone layer, which blocks harmful UV rays from the Sun.
False 1: Ozone is a two-atom oxygen molecule that blocks harmful UV rays from the Sun.
False 2: The ozone layer blocks harmful cosmic rays and solar wind from the Sun.

Chapter: 8th Ch13 - Our Home: Earth, a Unique Life Sustaining Planet
True Statement: Earth's magnetic field acts as a protective shield, pushing away high-energy particles (cosmic rays and solar wind) that could damage the atmosphere and reduce the ozone layer.
False 1: Earth's ozone layer acts as a protective shield, pushing away cosmic rays and solar wind.
False 2: Earth's magnetic field allows cosmic rays and solar wind to pass through freely without affecting the atmosphere.

Chapter: 8th Ch13 - Our Home: Earth, a Unique Life Sustaining Planet
True Statement: Cosmic rays are high-energy particles that come from far across the universe; solar wind particles come from the Sun.
False 1: Cosmic rays come from the Sun; solar wind particles come from far across the universe.

Chapter: 8th Ch13 - Our Home: Earth, a Unique Life Sustaining Planet
True Statement: The atmosphere, hydrosphere (water), geosphere (solid parts: rocks, soil, minerals), and biosphere (all living things) together sustain life on Earth.
False 1: Only the atmosphere and biosphere sustain life; hydrosphere and geosphere are not essential.

Chapter: 8th Ch13 - Our Home: Earth, a Unique Life Sustaining Planet
True Statement: All the water on Earth — in ponds, lakes, rivers, seas, oceans, and groundwater — together forms the hydrosphere.
False 1: All the water on Earth together forms the geosphere.

Chapter: 8th Ch13 - Our Home: Earth, a Unique Life Sustaining Planet
True Statement: Soil is rich in nutrients like nitrogen and potassium needed for plant growth; these come from the slow breakdown of rocks and the remains of plants and animals.
False 1: Soil nutrients (nitrogen and potassium) come from the atmosphere, not from rocks or plant remains.

Chapter: 8th Ch13 - Our Home: Earth, a Unique Life Sustaining Planet
True Statement: The variety of landforms, rocks, soils, and processes on Earth is called geodiversity; it creates unique habitats where different types of life can thrive.
False 1: The variety of landforms, rocks, and soils on Earth is called biodiversity.

Chapter: 8th Ch13 - Our Home: Earth, a Unique Life Sustaining Planet
True Statement: All living beings along with the places where they live make up the biosphere.
False 1: All living beings along with the places where they live make up the geosphere.

Chapter: 8th Ch13 - Our Home: Earth, a Unique Life Sustaining Planet
True Statement: Reproduction ensures the continuity of life on Earth; parents pass on genetic material (genes) to offspring.
False 1: Decomposition ensures the continuity of life on Earth.

Chapter: 8th Ch13 - Our Home: Earth, a Unique Life Sustaining Planet
True Statement: Genes are stored inside every cell of a living being and contain instructions for how the organism should develop.
False 1: Genes are stored only in the egg cell of a living being, not in every cell.

Chapter: 8th Ch13 - Our Home: Earth, a Unique Life Sustaining Planet
True Statement: In asexual reproduction, a single parent produces new individuals that are exact copies of itself.
False 1: In sexual reproduction, a single parent produces new individuals that are exact copies of itself.

Chapter: 8th Ch13 - Our Home: Earth, a Unique Life Sustaining Planet
True Statement: In sexual reproduction, instructions from two parents combine to create offspring that share traits with both parents but also show differences.
False 1: In asexual reproduction, instructions from two parents combine to create offspring that show differences from both parents.

Chapter: 8th Ch13 - Our Home: Earth, a Unique Life Sustaining Planet
True Statement: In vegetative propagation, any part of a plant — leaf, stem, or root — can be planted in soil to grow into a new plant.
False 1: In vegetative propagation, new plants can only grow from seeds, not from other plant parts.

Chapter: 8th Ch13 - Our Home: Earth, a Unique Life Sustaining Planet
True Statement: Single-celled organisms like bacteria and amoeba reproduce asexually by dividing into two identical individuals.
False 1: Single-celled organisms like bacteria and amoeba reproduce sexually by combining instructions from two individuals.

Chapter: 8th Ch13 - Our Home: Earth, a Unique Life Sustaining Planet
True Statement: Hydra grows tiny buds on its body that break off and grow into new individuals.
False 1: Planaria grows tiny buds on its body that break off and grow into new individuals.

Chapter: 8th Ch13 - Our Home: Earth, a Unique Life Sustaining Planet
True Statement: Planaria, a type of flatworm, can regrow from a small fragment of its body.
False 1: Hydra, a simple animal, can regrow from a small fragment of its body.

Chapter: 8th Ch13 - Our Home: Earth, a Unique Life Sustaining Planet
True Statement: In flowers, pollen grains found in the anther are the male gametes; ovules found deep inside the flower are the female gametes.
False 1: In flowers, pollen grains found in the anther are the female gametes; ovules found deep inside the flower are the male gametes.

Chapter: 8th Ch13 - Our Home: Earth, a Unique Life Sustaining Planet
True Statement: Fertilisation occurs when male and female gametes combine to form a zygote (which becomes the seed); the fleshy part of the flower around the ovule develops into a fruit.
False 1: Fertilisation is the process of carrying pollen from stamen to carpel.
False 2: The fleshy part around the ovule develops into the seed; the zygote becomes the fruit.

Chapter: 8th Ch13 - Our Home: Earth, a Unique Life Sustaining Planet
True Statement: In fish and frogs, fertilisation takes place in water and the development of the zygote into an embryo also takes place in water.
False 1: In fish and frogs, fertilisation takes place inside the body of the female.

Chapter: 8th Ch13 - Our Home: Earth, a Unique Life Sustaining Planet
True Statement: In birds, the fertilised egg (zygote) is laid by the female and the development of the zygote into an embryo takes place outside the body during hatching.
False 1: In birds, the development of the zygote into an embryo takes place inside the body of the female.

Chapter: 8th Ch13 - Our Home: Earth, a Unique Life Sustaining Planet
True Statement: In most mammals, the development of the zygote into an embryo takes place inside the body of the female.
False 1: In most mammals, the development of the zygote takes place in a laid egg outside the body.

Chapter: 8th Ch13 - Our Home: Earth, a Unique Life Sustaining Planet
True Statement: The biggest environmental challenges are climate change, biodiversity loss, and pollution — together called the triple planetary crisis.
False 1: The biggest environmental challenges are climate change, ozone depletion, and water scarcity — together called the triple planetary crisis.

Chapter: 8th Ch13 - Our Home: Earth, a Unique Life Sustaining Planet
True Statement: Burning fossil fuels like coal and oil releases greenhouse gases (carbon dioxide and methane) that trap heat in the atmosphere and cause global warming.
False 1: Burning fossil fuels reduces greenhouse gases (carbon dioxide and methane) in the atmosphere.

Chapter: 8th Ch13 - Our Home: Earth, a Unique Life Sustaining Planet
True Statement: The Montreal Protocol (1987) helped reduce harmful chemicals like CFCs (Chlorofluorocarbons), allowing the ozone layer to slowly recover.
False 1: The Kyoto Protocol (1987) helped reduce CFCs, allowing the ozone layer to slowly recover.
False 2: The Montreal Protocol (2005) helped reduce CFCs, allowing the ozone layer to slowly recover.

Chapter: 8th Ch13 - Our Home: Earth, a Unique Life Sustaining Planet
True Statement: The Paris Agreement (2015) committed countries to limit global warming to below 1.5°C.
False 1: The Kyoto Protocol (2015) committed countries to limit global warming to below 1.5°C.
False 2: The Paris Agreement (2015) committed countries to limit global warming to below 3°C.
